channel.title: OAM reference: contributor notes :: Go Kure — Launcher
channel.description: Each page here belongs to one part of the OAM and component reference (api-reference/oam and api-reference/oam-components). It holds what a contributor needs and a reader of the reference does not: the code that implements an entry, the issues behind it, and the tests that hold its claims. A page is named after its reference part and has one section per entry, with up to three lists: Implementation: the helper or file that builds the entry. History: the issues that introduced or changed it. Tests: the tests that hold a claim of the reference, with the claim each one holds. Text on these pages is moved from the reference without rewording. A claim stays in the reference; its test or issue reference moves here.

item.title: Policy defaults, endpoints and outputs
item.description: Implementation, history and tests of the sections on the reference page Policy defaults, endpoints and outputs. Text in square brackets is added here to say what a moved sentence refers to. Policy defaults & enforcement ordering Implementation: enforce.go’s applyDefaultQuantity [“fills any request/limit the author left unset”, in the reference’s tier 2.] oam.PolicyDefaultReporter: the workload kinds, cnpg-cluster, persistentvolumeclaim and the pvc trait embed an oam.PolicyDefaultLog; the scaler trait implements the interface itself, so that its config stays comparable [“is reported to the provenance report as a policy entry”, in the reference’s tier 2.] oam.BuiltinDefaultReporter, embedded oam.BuiltinDefaultLog in cnpg-cluster [“is reported as a builtin entry”, in the reference’s tier 2.] common.go ["buildResourceRequirements", in the reference’s tier 3.] capPolicyRequestDefaults, resource_policy_defaults.go [“held to the authored limit for that resource”, in the reference’s tier 3.] enforceMaxResources (enforce.go) closes this by calling the same buildResourceRequirements the generator calls, enforcing against its result, and discarding it — buildResourceRequirements deep-copies its maps, so this is read-only and generated output is unchanged. [“this” is the gap described in the History entry below it.] cnpgResourceList [“copies every entry of c.Resources straight onto the Cluster spec”, in the reference’s sentence on postgresql.] common.go’s buildResourceRequirements call sites at the init-container and sidecar builders [“receive the same intrinsic defaults”, in the reference’s paragraph on init containers and sidecars.] enforce.go [“the shared enforceExtraContainer helper”, in the same paragraph.] common.go [“a dedicated JobSpecConfig/parseJobSpec/applyJobSpec”, in the reference’s paragraph on the twelve JobSpec-level properties.] applyJobSpec copies every value it writes rather than assigning the config’s own pointers (copyPtr for the scalars, DeepCopy for successPolicy and podFailurePolicy, which each own a slice of rules). A handler config outlives one Generate call and Generate may run more than once, so an aliased pointer would leave a mutable path from the generated object back into the config — a writer through the object would change what the next Generate emits. History: go-kure/launcher#1181 [“an authored opt-out”, in the reference’s tier 1.] go-kure/launcher#1217; the apiserver refuses a request above its limit [“renders a 64Mi request, not 128Mi”, in the reference’s tier 3.] Prior to go-kure/launcher#251 the enforcement check ran before the intrinsic tier was computed, so an application that omitted spec.resources entirely could ship a Deployment whose 100m CPU / 128Mi memory intrinsic defaults exceeded the enforced maximum. [“the enforcement check” is the check of oam.Policy.MaxCPU()/MaxMemory() described in the reference’s paragraph on the effective value.] go-kure/launcher#312 ["ApplyPolicy enforces them too", in the reference’s paragraph on init containers and sidecars.] go-kure/launcher#344 ["job onto its own spec", in the reference’s paragraph on the twelve JobSpec-level properties.] Tests: Both halves are pinned: TestSchemaJobSpec_HasNoSuspendKey on the schema, TestCronjobHandler_SuspendWritesCronJobSpecOnly and TestJobHandler_SuspendWritesJobSpec on the generated objects. [“Both halves” are the two halves described in the reference’s paragraph “One JobSpec field is deliberately not shared: suspend”.] Policy refusal classes Implementation: enforce.go, enforcePodTemplatePolicy, enforceRenderedObjectPolicy [“one check raises it”, in the reference’s first bullet.] History: go-kure/launcher#849 [“instead of matching text”, in the reference’s first paragraph.] Pod view of a monitoring workload object (MonitoringPodSpec) History: go-kure/launcher#974 [“finds none to scan”, in the reference’s first paragraph.] Tests: Each monitoring workload kind adds its case from its own monitoringWorkload mapping; TestMonitoringPodSpec_CoversEveryRegisteredWorkloadKind (pkg/oam/builtin/registry) fails on a registered kind of the operator’s API whose spec lists containers and that has no case. [“its own monitoringWorkload mapping” is also “the same mapping” in the reference’s bullet “What it holds”.] Declared endpoints of a chart Implementation: chartEndpoints [“One shared schema and parser”, in the reference’s first paragraph.] History: go-kure/launcher#1132 [“implement oam.EndpointProvider from an endpoints property”, in the reference’s first paragraph.] Tests: the schema-parity test names endpoints as its one exception ["helmrelease decodes the rest as its HelmReleaseSpec", in the reference’s bullet “Not a chart value”.] Declared outputs History: go-kure/launcher#1259 [“implement oam.OutputProvider”, in the reference’s first paragraph.]

item.title: Kinds: networking

(“The list of a rule” is the reference’s “Required” list of the fields the CRD requires inside a rule, with the two more it names; “it” after “reads” is that list, and “it publishes” is the cilium-networkpolicy trait.) History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projection). go-kure/launcher#883 (the list of a rule’s required fields is kept by hand, not generated). Tests: TestCiliumNetworkPolicy_RequiredMatchCRD holds the whole list to the CiliumNetworkPolicy CRD of the linked module, its own file and not the cluster-wide policy’s, and to the rule type, under spec and under specs, so a dependency bump that adds, drops or moves one fails there. (“the whole list” is the reference’s “Required” list, the 59 fields and the two more it names, and “one” is a field of that list; the test is in cilium_networkpolicy_internal_test.go.) The positions are found from the Cilium types, and a test fails when a Cilium bump adds a type that unmarshals itself and is not checked. (“The positions” are the positions the reference’s previous sentence lists, those that hold a selector and the two other types under a rule that unmarshal themselves; the sentence names no test.) servicecidr History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projection). poddisruptionbudget History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projection). endpointslice History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projection). Tests: TestKindComponents_OmittedRequiredAndWrittenDefaults holds the kind in its table as well, from the same markers: to that, and to no default marked on a field the type writes unauthored. (“as well” is as TestBuiltinMarkerKinds_RequiredMatchMarkers holds the kind, which the reference names; “the same markers” are the +required and +optional markers of the linked k8s.io/api module named there; “that” is the reference’s “The API marks no field of the kind required that the type leaves out when unauthored”; the test is in kind_api_sets_internal_test.go.) cilium-bgpadvertisement, cilium-bgpclusterconfig, cilium-bgpnodeconfigoverride, cilium-bgppeerconfig Implementation: Each is built on policyFreeKind and emits that one object, named after the component unless objectName names it; the handler adds no label, no annotation and no default. (“Each” is each of the four kinds, cilium-bgpadvertisement, cilium-bgpclusterconfig, cilium-bgpnodeconfigoverride and cilium-bgppeerconfig, and “that one object” is the Cilium object the kind is the projection of.) History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projections). go-kure/launcher#922 (the object kind policy, oam.ObjectKindPolicy). go-kure/launcher#883 (the required lists are generated from the linked module’s v2 CRDs). The same test holds each checked rule to the API server’s own expression validator, run over the linked CRD after the defaults the API server fills: it refuses the properties that break the rule, by that rule alone, and accepts the ones next to them, and the kind answers the same on both. (“The same test” is TestCiliumBGPKinds_ExpressionRules, which the reference’s previous sentence names and which is in cilium_bgp_kinds_internal_test.go; “it” is the API server’s own expression validator, and “both” are the properties that break the rule and the ones next to them.) cilium-cidrgroup, cilium-loadbalancerippool, cilium-egressgatewaypolicy, cilium-localredirectpolicy, cilium-nodeconfig Implementation: Each is built on policyFreeKind and emits that one object, named after the component unless objectName names it; the handler adds no label, no annotation and no default of its own. (“Each” is each of the five kinds, cilium-cidrgroup, cilium-loadbalancerippool, cilium-egressgatewaypolicy, cilium-localredirectpolicy and cilium-nodeconfig, and “that one object” is the Cilium object the kind is the projection of.) History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projections). go-kure/launcher#922 (the object kind policy, oam.ObjectKindPolicy). go-kure/launcher#883 (the required lists are generated from the linked module’s v2 CRDs). Tests: TestCiliumPlainKinds_NoDefaultIsLost holds the defaults of the linked CRDs to that: one that is not the field’s empty value, on a field that is no pointer, fails there. (“that” is the reference’s “each of the three has that empty value as its default in the CRD”, “one” is a default of the linked CRDs, and the test is in cilium_plain_kinds_internal_test.go.) TestCiliumPlainKinds_RedirectFrontendTakesOneMatcher holds the check to the CRD, and fails where another schema of the five gains such a choice. (“the check” is the reference’s refusal of a redirectFrontend that authors neither or both of addressMatcher and serviceMatcher, “the five” are the five kinds of this entry, and the test is in cilium_plain_kinds_internal_test.go.) cilium-clusterwidenetworkpolicy History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projection). Tests: TestCoreKindSchemas_CoverSpec holds the two keys to the linked CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy type. (“the two keys” are spec and specs, the two fields the reference names as the component’s properties; the test is in core_kinds_test.go.) TestCiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy_ObjectRule holds the refusal to the API server’s own expression validator, which accepts an authored specs: [] and would refuse the object written without it; (“the refusal” is the refusal of no rule at all that the reference’s bullet states, and “it” is specs: []; the test is in cilium_clusterwidenetworkpolicy_internal_test.go.) TestCiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy_RequiredMatchCRD holds the whole list to the CRD of the linked module and to the rule type, under spec and under specs, so a dependency bump that adds, drops or moves one fails there. (“the whole list” is the reference’s “Required” list, the 59 fields and the two more it names, and “one” is a field of that list; the test is in cilium_clusterwidenetworkpolicy_internal_test.go.) TestCiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy_SchemaChoices lists every choice and expression rule of the linked CRD as checked or left, and fails on one that is neither; (“one” is a choice or an expression rule of the linked CRD that is neither checked nor left; the test is in cilium_clusterwidenetworkpolicy_internal_test.go.) gatewayclass, gateway, listenerset, referencegrant, backendtlspolicy Implementation: Each is built on policyFreeKind (see the storageclass entry) and emits that one object, named after the component unless objectName names it; the handler adds no label, no annotation and no default. (“Each” is each of the five kinds, gatewayclass, gateway, listenerset, referencegrant and backendtlspolicy, “that one object” is the Gateway API object the kind is the projection of, and “the storageclass entry” is on the reference page Kinds: core workloads.) History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projections). go-kure/launcher#922 (the object kind policy, oam.ObjectKindPolicy). go-kure/launcher#883 (the required lists are generated from the CRDs the linked module ships). Tests: TestGatewayKinds_DefaultedZeros holds each kind’s list of such fields to the numbers, booleans and strings that are omitted when zero and that a CRD of either channel defaults to something else. (“such fields” are the fields of these types that are omitted when zero or empty, as the reference’s previous sentences name them; the test is in gateway_kinds_internal_test.go.) TestKindComponents_OmittedRequiredAndWrittenDefaults derives that set from the CRDs, at every depth of the five specs, and holds each member to one of two answers: the kind’s refusal, which it runs, or a stated reason the decoded value cannot show the omission. (“that set” is the seven required fields the type omits that the reference lists under “A required field the type omits is refused by the kind itself”, and “the five specs” are the specs of the five kinds; the test is in kind_api_sets_internal_test.go.) None has the second answer. (“None” is none of the members of that set, and “the second answer” is the stated reason the decoded value cannot show the omission.) TestGatewayKinds_RefusedOmissions holds each refused field to being required in both channels, or, for a field only the experimental channel holds (the filter’s protocol), in that channel. (“each refused field” is each of those seven fields; the test is in gateway_kinds_internal_test.go.) tcproute, udproute, tlsroute Implementation: Each is built on policyFreeKind (above), as the kinds of the API’s infrastructure objects are, and emits that one object in the build namespace, named after the component unless objectName names it; the handler adds no label, no annotation and no default. (“Each” is tcproute, udproute and tlsroute; “(above)” is the storageclass entry that the entry for gatewayclass, gateway, listenerset, referencegrant and backendtlspolicy above names, and which is on the reference page Kinds: core workloads; “the kinds of the API’s infrastructure objects” are those five kinds; “that one object” is the Gateway API object the kind is the projection of.) History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projections). Tests: TestGatewayRouteKinds_OmissionsAreTheAPIServers and TestGatewayRouteKinds_ExpressionRules go one step further: they run the CRD of each channel through the API server’s own creation path (defaulting, the schema, the expression rules), and hold each refusal of a kind to a refusal of that path, and the object the kind emits for an accepted route to being accepted there. (“one step further” is further than the reference’s “the refused omissions are held to them”, “they” are the two tests this sentence names, and “that path” and “there” are the API server’s creation path; both tests are in gateway_route_kinds_internal_test.go.) The second names every expression rule a CRD declares: the one above, which it shows with routes that break it and routes that keep it, or a rule left to the API server with its reason. (“The second” is TestGatewayRouteKinds_ExpressionRules, “a CRD” is a CRD of either channel, “the one above” is the reference’s rule that a Service backend must name its port, and “it” is that test.) A dependency bump that adds or rewrites a rule fails there. (“there” is TestGatewayRouteKinds_ExpressionRules, the test the previous sentence calls “The second”.)

item.title: Kinds: Flux
item.description: Implementation, history and tests of the entries on the reference page Kinds: Flux. Every test named here is in pkg/oam/builtin/components/flux_kinds_internal_test.go unless a line says another file. fluxcd-alert, fluxcd-provider, fluxcd-receiver, imagepolicy, imagerepository, imageupdateautomation, artifactgenerator, resourcesetinputprovider Implementation: Each is built on policyFreeKind (see the storageclass entry) with the Flux namespace, the check of its durations and, where a field names a host the environment policy holds or holds a credential, a check under that policy (fluxKind), and emits that one object, named after the component unless objectName names it; the handler adds no label, no annotation and no default. (“the storageclass entry” is on the reference page Kinds: core workloads.) History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projections). go-kure/launcher#601 (a duration is held to the pattern its field declares). go-kure/launcher#619 (a timeout of an hour or more is written in minutes, as the timeout of a Flux source is). go-kure/launcher#984 (a Receiver resource’s apiVersion is checked at build time). go-kure/launcher#1010 (the version the refusal names for a kind outside the Receiver API’s kind enum). go-kure/launcher#883 (the Required lists are generated from the markers of the Go source, and the CRDs are vendored for the tests). go-kure/launcher#874 (a kind checks an expression rule only where the check is held to the API server’s own validator, which answers from a CRD). go-kure/launcher#975 (a pagerduty Provider’s routing key in channel). go-kure/launcher#1079 (a trait in a later group that makes a required read is refused). Tests: TestFluxKinds_DefaultedZeros holds each kind’s list of such fields to the numbers, booleans and strings that are omitted when zero and that the API defaults to something else. (“such fields” are the reference’s fields that the type omits when empty and the API defaults, as eventSeverity and filter.limit.) TestFluxKinds_MarkersClassified fails on a field the type writes unauthored that neither a marker nor that rule classifies. (“that rule” is the reference’s “schema generators’ rule” for a field with no marker whose json tag keeps it when empty.) A dependency bump that adds, drops or moves one fails there. (“there” is TestFluxKinds_MarkersClassified, and “one” is a field the type writes unauthored that a marker or that rule classifies.) TestKindComponents_GeneratedRequiredBothWays (the test the reference’s “the list of a resourcesetinputprovider is derived from its CRD instead, and held to that CRD by the API server” names; it is in kind_required_internal_test.go). The other kinds here are held to the API server’s own validator on the controllers’ CRDs, vendored from each controller’s repository at the tag of the linked API module, unmodified but for allow-term pragma comment lines (see “Vendored CRDs” under the required fields) (testdata/upstream/<repository>/, scripts/vendor-flux-crds.sh, each file checked against its git blob id by TestVendoredCRDs_MatchSource): of every type that holds a generated path, the same test creates the object with one such path authored, which the API server accepts, and without it, which the API server refuses as missing a required field; and every generated path is one the CRD declares. (“The other kinds here” are the kinds of the reference entry other than resourcesetinputprovider; “the required fields” are the reference’s Required fields a kind writes unauthored and does not refuse; “the same test” is TestKindComponents_GeneratedRequiredBothWays, which is in kind_required_internal_test.go; TestVendoredCRDs_MatchSource, which checks each vendored file, is in vendored_crds_internal_test.go.) TestFluxKinds_ExpressionRules reads every such rule from the markers of the linked source and holds the list (fluxRulesLeft) to them, and TestFluxOperatorKinds_ExpressionRulesMatchCRD holds the ResourceSetInputProvider’s list to the x-kubernetes-validations of the shipped CRD, in both directions, so a dependency bump that adds, drops or rewords one fails there. (“such rule”, “the list” and “one” are the API expression rules the reference lists under “The APIs’ expression rules are not checked”; “the ResourceSetInputProvider’s list” is its seventeen rules.) TestProviderAddressCredentialTypes_InUpstreamEnum holds the list to the API’s values of type. (“the list” is the reference’s list of Provider types whose address is the credential, or can be; the test is in fluxcd_provider_internal_test.go.) fluxcd-kustomization History: go-kure/launcher#784 (the kind-named terminal for Flux’s Kustomization). go-kure/launcher#352 (the type is fluxcd-kustomization rather than kustomization). go-kure/launcher#883 (the Required list of the fields the type writes unauthored is generated from the markers of the linked kustomize-controller module). go-kure/launcher#740 (FluxNamespaceReads: the ConfigMaps and Secrets it reads from its own namespace). go-kure/launcher#1079 (a trait in a later group that makes a required read is refused). Tests: a test ties the published schema to that struct, so a bump that adds or drops a spec field fails the suite until the schema follows. (“that struct” is KustomizationSpec, of the reference’s “Its properties are exactly the top-level JSON keys of KustomizationSpec”; the sentence names no test.) helmrepository, ocirepository, gitrepository, bucket, helmchart History: go-kure/launcher#347 (the kind-named terminals for Flux’s four fetching source kinds, part of the Helm-family redesign go-kure/launcher#336). go-kure/launcher#351 (helmchart, the kind that builds a chart artifact from one of them). go-kure/launcher#1078 (a url must not carry a credential). go-kure/launcher#601 (an interval is checked as on helmrelease). go-kure/launcher#606 (the timeout pattern of the source CRDs has no h unit). go-kure/launcher#619 (a timeout of an hour or more is emitted with its hours folded into minutes). go-kure/launcher#790 (an authored verify that names no provider is written with provider: cosign, and an authored provider: "" is refused). go-kure/launcher#883 (every other required field the type writes unauthored is refused, from a list generated from the markers of the linked source-controller module). go-kure/launcher#699 (no refusal prints the value it refused). go-kure/launcher#740 (FluxNamespaceReads: the Secrets and the ConfigMap a reference names move with the source). go-kure/launcher#1079 (a trait in a later group that makes a required read is refused). Tests: a test ties each published schema to its struct, so a bump that adds or drops a spec field fails the suite until the schema follows. (“its struct” is the source-controller spec type of the reference’s “Each component’s properties are exactly the top-level JSON keys of its source-controller spec type”; the sentence names no test.) A reflection test asserts, per kind, that no spec field is unreachable through that decode, against an explicit exclusion list that is empty. (“that decode” is the strict decode of the reference’s “Decoding”.)

item.title: Kinds: MetalLB
item.description: Implementation, history and tests of the entries on the reference page Kinds: MetalLB. Every test named here is in pkg/oam/builtin/components/metallb_kinds_internal_test.go unless a line says another file. metallb-bfdprofile Implementation: built on policyFreeKind (see the storageclass entry on the reference page Kinds: core workloads), and emits that one object. History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projection); go-kure/launcher#922 (the object kind policy, oam.ObjectKindPolicy). Tests: TestMetalLBKinds_NoDefaultIsLost fails on a default a dependency bump adds to a field that could not carry an authored empty value. TestMetalLBKinds_RequiredMatchCRD holds that to the linked module’s v1beta1 CRD (“that” is the reference’s “Required: nothing”). The CRD declares none; TestMetalLBKinds_ExpressionRules fails on one that is added (“none” is the CRD’s expression rules). metallb-bgpadvertisement Implementation: built on policyFreeKind as metallb-bfdprofile is, and emits that one object. History: go-kure/launcher#790 (the kind-named projection); go-kure/launcher#883 (the Required list is generated from the linked module’s v1beta1 CRD); go-kure/launcher#922 (the object kind policy). Tests: TestMetalLBKinds_NoDefaultIsLost holds the defaults of the linked CRD to that (“that” is the reference’s account of the two aggregation lengths: pointers, whose API defaults are 32 and 128, one route per address). TestMetalLBKinds_RequiredMatchCRD holds it to that CRD as well (“it” is the Required list, generated from the linked module’s v1beta1 CRD). TestMetalLBKinds_ExpressionRules holds the kind’s answer to the API server’s for the linked CRD, on properties that break the rule and on properties that keep it, and fails on a rule that is added or reworded. metallb-bgppeer Implementation: built on policyHeldKind, the helper of policyFreeKind with one check under the environment policy, and emits that one object. item.title: The null contract and two spellings of one field
item.description: Implementation, history and tests of the sections on the reference page The null contract and two spellings of one field. Text in square brackets is added here to say what a moved sentence refers to. The null contract Implementation: authoredValue — the presence primitive parseStringField, parseObjectField, parseInt32Field, parseInt64Field, parseObjectList and parseStringList all go through — does exactly that, so calling any of them directly already complies. They classify a typed nil as null too — map[string]any(nil) or []any(nil) inside an any, which is what a lowering rule assembled in Go produces for an unset optional and is not == nil. [“that” is the reference’s “read a null under an optional property as omission”; “They” are the six helpers named in this sentence.] A new optional field is read with the helper for its type instead: parseStringField (or requiredStringField when the field is required), parseBoolField, parseInt32Field, parseInt64Field, parseObjectField, parseObjectList or parseStringList. Each already reads an explicit null as absence through authoredValue, so a wrapper would only repeat that check. [“instead” is instead of an optional* wrapper; “a wrapper” is one of those, listed under History.] History: It is written down because “null” has several readers — the emission validator’s requiredness check and its optional-key strip, its array-element guard, enforcePlatformReserved, this package’s parsers, and the Kubernetes API itself — and each was aligned separately, so each round of review found the reader the last round had not touched. [“It” is the reference’s rule on the null contract.] This used to require a separate optional* wrapper family (optionalString, optionalObject, optionalInt32, optionalInt64, optionalObjectList, optionalStringList) layered in front of the plain parsers. go-kure/launcher#394 moved the handling into the shared helpers themselves, which made every wrapper an exact no-op forward; they were removed and every caller now uses the parse* helper directly. go-kure/launcher#423, go-kure/launcher#394 and go-kure/launcher#570 converted the parsers they covered; the last of them are listed with the null row of the deployment table above. [“the parsers they covered” are the parsers that answer presence with a bare v, ok := props[key], the first limit of the reference; “the deployment table above” is on the reference page of the deployment kind.] Both limits met on one key, and it was the second row of that table. namespaceSelector is parsed twice in this repository: here, for pod affinity, through parseSchedulingSelector (parseObjectField), where any null is omission — which upstream reads as “this pod’s namespace”; and in the networkpolicy trait, through parseNPPeer. A typed nil used to satisfy the networkpolicy trait’s own type assertion and yield an empty selector — all namespaces, the widest possible answer — while an untyped nil already read as omission there, so one input landed on opposite ends of the range depending on which Go nil shape produced it. Both parsers now route their presence check through oam.IsNullValue’s reflect-based classification, which treats a typed nil the same as an untyped one, so the two halves converge: a null namespaceSelector, however it was constructed, is omission on both paths. [“Both limits” are the two limits the reference lists; “that table” is its labelSelector and namespaceSelector table; “here” is the handler parsers.] The same typed-nil shape reached list elements. parseObjectList read a null key as absence, but a typed-nil element ([]any{map[string]any(nil)}) passed its per-element assertion as an empty object, where an untyped null element is refused (tolerations[0]: must be an object, got <nil>). Most callers then failed on a missing required field anyway. tolerations did not: an empty entry became an Exists toleration with no key, which tolerates every taint. The element is now normalised to a null first, so every caller refuses both shapes identically (go-kure/launcher#465). The list readers that do not go through parseObjectList (envFrom, httpHeaders, volumes, volumeMounts, sidecar ports, the Job successPolicy/podFailurePolicy rules and onPodConditions, volumeClaimTemplates, valuesFrom, scopeOverrides) pass each element through nullElem first, for the same untyped refusal and message. [“The same typed-nil shape” is the one of the entry above.] Tests: TestNoOptionalFieldWrappers (no_optional_wrappers_internal_test.go) keeps them removed: it fails on any function or method whose name starts with optional. It parses every production .go file directly in this package’s directory — every file, not only common.go, and never a _test.go file or a subdirectory — and fails if it parsed none, so a wrong working directory cannot pass it vacuously. [“them” are the optional* wrappers of the History entry above.] Fixed as go-kure/launcher#430; networkpolicy_internal_test.go’s TestParseNPPeer_NamespaceSelectorPresenceCases pins the typed-nil case directly. [“Fixed” is the namespaceSelector split of the History entry that starts “Both limits”.] Two spellings of one field Implementation: foldedKey [the helper behind the reference’s sentence on the helmrelease verify check that still refuses a pair in which one spelling is null, which the decode lets through]. History: Before, those documents built. [“those documents” are the ones a kind that decodes by itself builds, listed in the reference’s gitrepository and helmrelease sentence.]

The hint was asked of a terminal component handler alone before go-kure/launcher#790; the three other positions are new. [The hint is UnsupportedFieldHint.] Before go-kure/launcher#790 a nested refusal carried no hint. go-kure/launcher#1466 (every refusal the property validators make is a *PropertyError). go-kure/launcher#1469 (the platform-reservation check is one of those refusals). go-kure/launcher#325 (the shape check is the only place an authored scalar’s type is enforced for every property). go-kure/launcher#1282 (the app argument is never edited, for a plain type name and for a declared type identity alike). go-kure/launcher#1463 (top-level Required is enforced as written, and a null counts as absent). go-kure/launcher#765 (nested Required, inside an object the author did write, is enforced). go-kure/launcher#750 (for a trait a binding matches, the check reads the trait’s properties as the rendering merges into them, recursively, so a required key the rendering supplies is not refused). Tests: A completeness test (pkg/cmd/kurel) enforces that every built-in schema node declares exactly one of Type and Types. A completeness test (pkg/cmd/kurel) enforces that no built-in schema node is left without a description. What an explicit null means on the emitted path History: go-kure/launcher#394 (aligning the parser-level layer with this contract, a separate, lower-level concern, is not closed by this). go-kure/launcher#431 (capability rendering, checkCapabilityValueType, now agrees with the contract’s own behaviour). go-kure/launcher#430 (the networkpolicy peer parser read a typed nil namespaceSelector differently from an untyped one; both parsers now route their presence check through oam.IsNullValue’s reflect-based classification). Tests: What is asserted is the rule above: TestBuiltinHandlerSchemaEnumMembersHoldNoNull (pkg/cmd/kurel) walks every schema that ships for a member holding a null, because the runtime arm only fires once a document validates against the property carrying the Enum. Lowering targets and Seal History: go-kure/launcher#789 (a consumer that registers a built-in lowering rule without the types it lowers into now fails at Seal, a breaking library change).

item.title: Component label and ownership
item.description: Implementation, history and tests of the sections on the reference page Component label and ownership. Text in square brackets is added here to say what a moved sentence refers to. Component label and ownership History: go-kure/launcher#788 (every application of a transformed document belongs to one authored component, or to the document as a whole). go-kure/launcher#783 (a generated source the application bundle holds, which every consumer shares, belongs to none: the document as a whole). go-kure/launcher#790 (the label is authoritative: before it writes the label, the wrapper holds every object the application generates to it). go-kure/launcher#1085 (the component label and reserved-key checks read a typed object in its JSON form with numbers kept exact, so a HelmRelease whose values hold a number no float64 holds is not refused for it). go-kure/launcher#944 (the StatefulSet volume claim templates, spec.volumeClaimTemplates[].metadata, are not read for the component label). go-kure/launcher#957 (the claim template of the storage of a Prometheus, PrometheusAgent, Alertmanager or ThanosRuler, spec.storage.volumeClaimTemplate.metadata, is not read for the component label). go-kure/launcher#788 (breaking library changes: every owned object and pod template gains the component label, a HelmRelease gains the post-renderer, and a component’s synthesized NetworkPolicies gain the label; a Job a cluster holds from before cannot take the label on its pod template; GeneratedApplication.Component changes; and stack.Application.Config is the ownership wrapper after Transform). go-kure/launcher#790 (the authoritative label, breaking library changes: a document that built before is refused at generation when an object it generates holds the component label’s key with a value that is not its component’s; under ComponentLabelKey: "app" what the built-in kinds and traits write still builds; and the reserved metadata keys are read in five more places, and in the metadata an operator copies onto objects it creates that are no pods, and in spec.commonMetadata of a Flux Kustomization, HelmRelease or ResourceSet). go-kure/launcher#790 (a CronJob’s job template, breaking library changes: every CronJob an owned application generates gains the component label on its job template, and a job template that holds a foreign value or a reserved metadata key is refused; new exported API ReservedKeyInJobTemplate). go-kure/launcher#790 (a selector that rules the label out, breaking library changes: an owned workload whose own selector rules the component label out of a pod template that carries no value for the key is refused, and so is one whose selector the check cannot read; new exported API ComponentLabelSelectorRulesOut). go-kure/launcher#790 (a renamed entry under the key app, breaking library changes: with ComponentLabelKey: "app" the synthesized inbound and egress NetworkPolicies of an entry a lowering rule emitted under a name whose label value differs from its component’s select app In [<component>, <entry>]). go-kure/launcher#790 (the authoritative label, new exported API: the sentinel ErrComponentLabelValue, the error type ComponentLabelError, the type ComponentLabelRefusal with four of its values, five values of ReservedKeyHolder, and the field ReservedMetadataKeyError.Path). go-kure/launcher#790 (metadata that reaches no pods, new exported API: nine values of ReservedKeyHolder). go-kure/launcher#944 (a StatefulSet’s volume claim templates, breaking library changes: a volume claim template that holds a reserved metadata key as a label or an annotation is refused at generation; new exported API ReservedKeyInVolumeClaimTemplate). go-kure/launcher#957 (a Prometheus operator kind’s storage claim template, breaking library changes: a storage claim template that holds a reserved metadata key is refused at generation, where neither spec.storage.emptyDir nor spec.storage.ephemeral is set; no new API). Tests: A test fails when the code asserts or switches on a new type directly on an application’s config (app.Config.(T), switch app.Config.(type)) and the wrapper’s list does not account for it. It reads syntax only: a config first copied to a variable or passed to a function, and asserted there, is outside what it sees. [“the wrapper” is launcher’s ownership wrapper, and “list” is configContracts in pkg/oam/component_ownership_test.go, which names each contract the wrapper forwards and, for each one it does not, why not.] labelReachReservedOnly in pkg/cmd/kurel/label_reach_test.go names each such field with what it reaches, and labelReachNotRead each field neither check reads. TestLabelReach_EveryFieldIsHeldOrListed derives these fields from the API types of the registered kind components, so a field a dependency adds fails the test until it is held or listed. [“such field” is a field of metadata that an operator copies onto other objects it creates, held to the reserved keys alone; “these fields” are the fields through which labels and annotations reach what the cluster creates from an object: those the two checks hold, and those the two names above list.] Reserved metadata keys History: go-kure/launcher#790 (TransformContext.ReservedMetadataKeys: one rule holds every application the transform returns to the list of reserved keys, whatever wrote the key). go-kure/launcher#944 (the metadata of each volume claim template of an apps StatefulSet is read for the reserved keys). go-kure/launcher#957 (the metadata of the storage claim template of a Prometheus, PrometheusAgent, Alertmanager or ThanosRuler is read for the reserved keys, where neither spec.storage.emptyDir nor spec.storage.ephemeral is set). go-kure/launcher#790 (library changes: the new exported field TransformContext.ReservedMetadataKeys, the sentinel ErrReservedMetadataKey, the error type ReservedMetadataKeyError with its ReservedKeyHolder values, and the method PlatformAnnotations() on the ingress trait’s config; breaking for documents: an expose trait whose authored annotation contradicts a value the trait writes is refused). Tests: labelReachNotRead in pkg/cmd/kurel/label_reach_test.go is the full list of fields of the kinds’ API types that hand metadata on and are not read. [“not read” is not read by either check.]
